releases.name: v0.24.0
releases.notes:
trust-manager is the easiest way to manage security-critical TLS trust bundles in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

This release is a feature release, but as usual, it contains various patches/fixes and dependency bumps.

Notable changes include a fix by @yugstar avoiding reconciling loops by ensuring the calculated trust bundle hash is deterministic when adding labels/annotations to the target configmaps/secrets. 💯 And trust-manager can now source CA certificates from configmap `binaryData`. 🚀 

Our Helm chart now supports configuration of securityContexts for pods and containers, which has been highly requested by the community. A big thanks goes out to @MarcAntoineRaymond! ❤️ 

⚠️ Possibly breaking change in Helm chart values: if you currently set `app.securityContext.seccompProfileEnabled`, this value has been removed and replaced with a more generic mechanism for setting securityContexts.

## What's Changed

### Features

* feat(helm)!: configuration of securityContexts for pods and containers by @MarcAntoineRaymond in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/836
* feat(helm): aggregate Bundle read access into the cluster-reader ClusterRole by @yugstar in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/1009
* Make CertPool support pluggable filters by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/1016
* feat: read CA data from ConfigMap binaryData field in Bundle sources by @mvanhorn in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/1025

### Fixes

* fix: scope metrics ServiceMonitor selector to the metrics service by @yugstar in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/1008

releases.name: v0.23.0
releases.notes:
trust-manager is the easiest way to manage security-critical TLS trust bundles in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

This release is a feature release, but as usual, it contains various patches/fixes and dependency bumps.

The most notable feature in this release is probably that trust-manager now provides a new trust-package bundle based on Debian Trixie.
💡  Note that the new `trust-pkg-debian-trixie` bundle is now the default trust package emitted by the Helm chart. For those of you still using our trust packages built from Debian Bullseye/Bookworm, we've just published new releases to fix vulnerabilites reported by scanners.

Our Helm chart has a new feature that allows a user to override the default webhook TLS certificate duration. We've also got a fix making it easier to use the trust-manager chart in an umbrella chart together with other cert-manager projects. This release also includes multiple fixes/inconsistencies in the Helm chart when using non-default values.

## What's Changed

### Features

* Add duration for the webhook tls certificate by @mvrk69 in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/961
* Add new trust package based on Debian Trixie by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/985
* Make new trust package based on Debian Trixie the new default by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/998

releases.name: v0.21.0
releases.notes:
trust-manager is the easiest way to manage security-critical TLS trust bundles in Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters.

This release is primarily intended to fix CVE-2025-68121, but it includes several changes which have trickled in since v0.20.3

## Notable Changes

### Filter Non-CA Certs in Sources

There's a new `.filterNonCACerts.enabled` value available in the Helm chart, which will cause trust-manager to filter any non-CA certs found in sources. This logic relies on the `isCa` field of the `basicConstraints` X.509 extension only. The feature defaults to "off".

### CRD Changes

The `ClusterBundle` CRD got a little stricter, to pass the Kube API Linter checks which we've enabled. We don't expect that this will change the use of the CRD for anyone, since the limits we've added are very permissive.

## What's Changed

### Functional / CRD Changes

* Add certificate verification process to filter non-CA certificates by @arsenalzp in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/824
* Helm Chart: Add support for setting relabelling on the ServiceMonitor by @tiesmaster in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/870
* Introduce Kube API linter by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/850
* Introduce KAL minlength/maxlength checks by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/866
* Introduce KAL required fields checks by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/877
* Fix index formatting in webhook validations by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/873
* Eliminate use of naked bool (includeDefaultCAs) in ClusterBundle API by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/855
* Enable the CommentStart KAL check and fix violations by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/858
* Rename ClusterBundle sources to sourceRefs by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/854

### Trust Packages

* Bump trust package versions to address CVE-2025-61729 by @SgtCoDFish in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/817
* Trigger a new build of default trust bundle images by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/875

### Tests / Docs

* Refactor Bundle integration tests by @erikgb in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/828

Furthermore, additional go dependencies were upgraded where possible.

* fix(deps): update module sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime to v0.22.3 by @octo-sts[bot] in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/773
* Bump trust package suffix, forcing a new go 1.25.3 build by @inteon in https://github.com/cert-manager/trust-manager/pull/776
